## SWE-bench Pro — decontaminated benchmark

Per Scale AI SEAL leaderboard summary [33]:

| Model | SWE-bench Pro (SEAL standardized scaffolding) |
|---|---|
| Claude Opus 4.5 | **45.9%** |
| Claude Sonnet 4.5 | 43.6% |

The Verified-vs-Pro gap on Opus 4.5: **80.9% → 45.9%, a ~35 percentage-point spread** [33]. SWE-bench Pro tasks modify "an average of 4.1 files" with "107.4 lines changed," vs single-file Verified tasks [33]. Same model varies 50.2-55.4% on Pro depending on agent framework — "the scaffolding gap is the most underappreciated finding" [33].

## Why SWE-bench Verified is being abandoned

OpenAI's retirement post (URL fetched but returned 403; supporting evidence in counter-perspective research and [33]):
- Contamination: every frontier model tested (GPT-5.2, Claude Opus 4.5, Gemini 3 Flash) could reproduce verbatim gold patches or problem statement specifics on Verified tasks [33].
- 35.5% of Verified tasks have "narrow tests" that reject functionally correct solutions; 18.8% have "wide tests" that check unspecified features [counter-perspective research].
- OpenAI found >60% of 138 analyzed problems were unsolvable or poorly constructed [counter-perspective research].

The "SWE-Bench Illusion" paper (arXiv:2506.12286, referenced via counter-perspective research) demonstrates 76% vs 53% file-path accuracy gap on in-benchmark vs out-of-benchmark repos and 35% vs 18% 5-gram verbatim similarity — direct evidence of memorization.

## Cursor's own benchmark

Cursor published Composer 2 results [8]:
- CursorBench: 61.3 (Composer 2) — Cursor's internal benchmark using Cursor Blame to trace committed code back to agent queries, intended to reduce contamination
- Terminal-Bench 2.0: 61.7 (vs Claude Opus 4.6 at 58.0; GPT-5.4 at 75.1)
- SWE-bench Multilingual: 73.7

These are vendor-published figures, not independently audited.

## Gemini cross-benchmark anomaly

- LiveCodeBench (contamination-resistant, competitive programming) — Gemini 3 Pro Preview reportedly leads at ~91.7% per third-party tracking [agent research]; live leaderboard fetch returned only loading scaffolding.
- SWE-bench Verified — Gemini does not place near the top [32].

The split is real and meaningful: LiveCodeBench rewards algorithmic / competitive programming skills (Gemini's strength), while SWE-bench rewards real-codebase patch application (Claude's strength). Treat any single benchmark as measuring a single capability, not "coding quality" abstractly.

## Real-world regression evidence

- **Cursor 2.1.50 (December 2025) [11]:** Multiple confirmed regressions including silent file emptying on save, sandbox network blocks, context loss between sessions. Cursor team acknowledged the network-sandbox bug; "fix in progress" status Dec 9, 2025; thread auto-closed Dec 31, 2025 with no follow-up resolution.
- **Gemini 2.5 Pro hallucination cascade [36]:** On a real SWE-bench task (astropy HTML writer `formats` argument), Gemini 2.5 Pro spent 39 turns and modified 693 lines without solving a 2-line bug. Fabricated `core.BaseWriter` class and `get_col_str_iters()` method; hallucinated terminal output and line numbers.
- **Claude Code token-consumption bug:** Discovery agent flagged versions v2.1.89 - v2.1.100 reportedly added ~20K invisible tokens per request, causing rate limits to be hit 3-50× faster. Anthropic acknowledged publicly March 31, 2026 [agent research, secondary source].
- **GitHub Copilot agent reliability complaints:** GitHub Discussions thread #170595 (Aug 2025) documents blank responses, hangs, infinite "continue" loops across multiple IDEs and models [counter-perspective research].

## Productivity studies

- **GitHub's own controlled study [16]:** n=95 developers, JavaScript HTTP server task. "55% faster than the developers who didn't use GitHub Copilot" with 95% CI [21%, 89%], P=.0017. Copilot group: 78% completion rate, 1h 11m average. Control: 70% completion, 2h 41m average. Funded by GitHub.

- **METR randomized controlled trial [34]:** 16 experienced open-source developers, 246 real GitHub issues, ~2 hours each. Result: developers using AI tools (primarily Cursor Pro + Claude 3.5/3.7 Sonnet) took **19% longer** to complete issues. Developers expected 24% speedup; even after experiencing slowdown, perceived 20% speedup. Compensation $150/hour; screen recordings used.

- **GitClear longitudinal analysis [35]:** 211M lines analyzed 2020-2024 across Google/Microsoft/Meta/enterprise repos. Code duplication rose 8.3% → 12.3% (~48% increase). Refactoring rate fell 25% (2021) → under 10% (2024). "Copy/pasted code exceeded moved code for the first time in history."

- **Pragmatic Engineer 2026 survey [37]:** n=906, Jan 27 – Feb 17, 2026. 95% use AI weekly+; 75% use AI for ≥50% of work; 56% do 70%+ work with AI. Tool ranking by mentions: Claude Code (1st), chatbots (2nd), GitHub Copilot (3rd), Cursor (4th), Codex (5th). 46% identify Claude Code as most-loved. Self-selected, experienced audience caveat acknowledged by authors.

The picture is consistent: vendor / self-report studies show large positive impact (55%+); independent randomized trials show null or negative impact at the individual-developer level; longitudinal repo data shows declining refactoring and rising duplication. The buyer is being asked to weigh self-perception (which is positive) against measured outcomes (which are mixed at best).

## Security and safety findings

- **45% of AI-generated code introduces OWASP Top 10 vulnerabilities** per Checkmarx (counter-perspective research; not directly fetched in-session). Specific 2025 CVEs: CVE-2025-54135 (Cursor RCE), CVE-2025-53109 (Anthropic MCP arbitrary file read/write), CVE-2025-55284 (Claude Code DNS exfiltration).
- **IBM Bob January 2026 vulnerabilities [30]:** PromptArmor research found Bob's CLI could be tricked into executing malware via process substitution bypass and `>` redirection chaining; the IDE had a zero-click data-exfiltration vector via markdown image rendering. Patched-before-GA status not confirmed in surfaced sources.
